races.name: Army Benevolent Fund/ebf Novice Stakes (gbb Race)
Hugh James Classified Stakes

runners_data.name: Iconic Times
runners_data.note: Modest recent form (0W0P in similar going) and limited seven-furlong record in this going profile; Sean Bowen provides a significant jockey upgrade but the horse's natural hold-up style means it needs things to fall right, and headgear (p) suggests connections are trying to find an answer.|

runners_data.name: Due Respect
runners_data.note: Clifford Lee rides for Gary Rutherford who has returned zero winners from six runners in the 14-day window; genuine hold-up horse whose best form at 7f on Good (two places from five runs) is solid, but will likely find itself shuffled into a midfield slot well ahead of its comfort zone given this race's rear-heavy composition.|

runners_data.name: Rain Cap
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old veteran who has one win and five places from nine similar-going runs, making him the most exposed but also the most reliable profile in the race; John David Riches has a quiet 14-day record and Ethan Tindall (5) claims, yet Rain Cap's tactical versatility means the understated pace of this race may not be as problematic for him as for some.|

runners_data.name: Wait For It
runners_data.note: Produced three places from seven runs on Good, including a recent 3rd and 2nd in 6-7f Good company, showing genuine form at the trip; Billy Garritty takes the ride for Liam Bailey, and while this horse functions best as a hold-up type, its recent 6f/7f pattern suggests it can at least travel closer to pace than its style tag implies if forced to.|

runners_data.name: Without Delay
runners_data.note: Tracy Waggott's seven-year-old has one win and three places from 12 Good-ground starts, demonstrating consistent if unspectacular form; coming into this race after 19 days off, it is a confirmed back-marker whose chance diminishes most sharply in a race where the tempo does not stretch the field into a line — Connor Beasley will face a stiff task generating momentum.|

runners_data.name: Ziva's Star
runners_data.note: Andrew Elliott rides for Simon Whitaker, who has produced no winners from six runners in the past fortnight; best form comes over 5-6f on Good, making this 7f trip a stamina query, and the horse's natural hold-up style is a further handicap in a race where it will struggle to find its ground.|

runners_data.name: Our Hero Matty
runners_data.note: The only front-runner in the field, giving Barry McHugh complete control of the pace on behalf of Tony Culhane & Stella Barclay; dropping back from sprint distances to 7f is a concern (best efforts have come at 5-6f) but the uncontested lead mitigates that risk, and the trainer's 14-day record (1/7) shows recent activity.|

races.paceDynamic: Our Hero Matty is the sole confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner field and, with no genuine rival to press him, Barry McHugh should be able to dictate a measured, sustainable gallop from the front over Catterick's flat seven furlongs. The remainder of the field — Due Respect, Wait For It, Without Delay, Ziva's Star, Iconic Times and Rain Cap — are all natural hold-up or rear-of-field types, meaning the pace is unlikely to be pressured and the leader will not be harried into early errors. This race shape heavily favours horses that can travel close to or just off a lone, uncontested lead rather than those who need a truly searching gallop to reel in the front-runner late. The field holds considerably more true hold-up types than the race map can accommodate at the rear — Due Respect, Wait For It, Without Delay and Ziva's Star are all genuine closers who are likely to find themselves in an unfamiliar midfield berth rather than their natural hunting ground, with Rain Cap and Iconic Times the most likely to organically settle closest to the pace without forcing the issue.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Lead Holds
scenarios.trigger: If Our Hero Matty is allowed to bowl along at a comfortable, uncontested gallop and the hold-up horses cannot generate momentum from an unpressured pace.
scenarios.body: Our Hero Matty dictates every yard at a tempo that suits him, and with the closers burning ground from wide or unfavourable positions, the leader simply has too much in hand entering the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closest Pursuers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely moderate and a horse travelling just off the leader — rather than the true hold-up types — gets a perfect split into the straight.
scenarios.body: A horse like Rain Cap or Wait For It, finding themselves closer to the pace than ideal for a hold-up type, benefits from a ground-saving position and produces a clean run through to challenge Our Hero Matty inside the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Land Blow
scenarios.trigger: If the uncontested gallop is faster than it appears and hold-up horses find late energy as the leader ties up in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: Due Respect or Without Delay, operating from their natural stalking position despite redistribution pressures, benefit if the field fans wide and gaps appear late — though their out-of-role mapping significantly limits this outcome.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses — Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Our Hero Matty sets an erratic or very slow pace that triggers a bunched finish with multiple challengers arriving together.
scenarios.body: The field concertinas approaching the final furlong and a horse like Iconic Times or Ziva's Star, who possess course-type profile and can quicken from a compact group, steals a march on those anchored wide.

watchPoints.text: Our Hero Matty controls the pace entirely — if Barry McHugh elects to go very steady early, the entire race becomes a sprint from the home turn and the hold-up brigade will have nothing to aim at.

Due Respect, Wait For It, Without Delay and Ziva's Star are all natural hold-up horses forced to race closer to the pace than they prefer — watch for traffic and positioning issues as they jostle for the same midfield ground in a small field.

Rain Cap's jockey, apprentice Ethan Tindall (5), claims 5lbs which is the most significant claim on the card — if Tindall times the run too late from Rain Cap's hold-up position, the uncontested leader will be untouchable.

Our Hero Matty steps up from its habitual 5-6f trip to 7f for the first time in this race — if the extra furlong proves beyond the horse's stamina in the closing stages, a closer like Wait For It (placed over 7f Good) is best positioned to capitalise.

races.name: Jacky Rylance 60th Birthday Celebration Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Free World
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer for Ian Williams whose recent form (form string shows fades) is a concern given the likely measured tempo; Cieren Fallon is a positive booking but the ⚠ fade tag and 0 wins from 6 similar-going runs suggests this race shape may expose the same weakness again.

runners_data.name: Karthala
runners_data.note: Consistent front-section traveller for Jennie Candlish with five places from 15 similar-going runs, racing 16f-20f on good — the 2m Catterick trip looks ideal; tongue-strap headgear applied, Sean D Bowen a strong jockey booking, and the 20-day break appears acceptable given recent activity.

runners_data.name: Fleur de Mer
runners_data.note: Martin Todhunter's 6yo wears a visor and has placed twice at 14f on Southwell's artificial surface but has only a 2/15 strike rate on comparable going — the surface switch to good turf is a notable question mark despite the course and distance of the trip suiting a hold-up profile.

runners_data.name: Zephlyn
runners_data.note: Ewan Whillans' 7yo wears a tongue-tie and, though a natural hold-up horse, is being relied upon to set the pace as the race's most likely front-runner; its 2W3P record from 7 similar-going runs shows it handles the conditions, but it will be racing out of its natural role at a likely cost to its finishing effort.

runners_data.name: Slack Alice
runners_data.note: Mickey Bowen's 5yo is a genuine stayer who has won over 22f and 23f on good ground — the 2m trip here is short of her best but she handles it; her true style is hold-up and she arrives here having been mapped to midfield, meaning she may not find the real position she needs to unleash her stamina-based finish.

runners_data.name: Speechman
runners_data.note: Philip Kirby's 6yo carries a tongue-tie and blinkers, and comes here on just four days' rest after a 7th at Carlisle — that quick turnaround with Kirby's 0/13 T14 stat demands caution; a natural closer whose map position overstates how close to the pace he will actually want to be.

runners_data.name: Lillistar
runners_data.note: Micky Hammond's 6yo has run into the places four times from 7 good-going runs and wears a hood; at 16 days since her last run she arrives fresh enough, and her 16f placed form is relevant — though her actual race position will be further back than the midfield map suggests, requiring daylight to emerge late.

runners_data.name: Star Of Jupiter
runners_data.note: Mark Loughnane's 5yo wears a tongue-tie plus best-equipment headgear and has three places on good ground at 14f-16f; William Pyle's claim is a factor, and while the 40-day absence is the longest in the field, the horse has placed coming fresh before — naturally a closer that will need traffic to clear.

runners_data.name: Ruler Of The River
runners_data.note: Philip Kirby's second runner, also a hold-up horse who has won over 12f on good and placed three times in similar conditions; just seven days since last run is fresh but manageable, and a tongue-tie plus hood combination could sharpen focus — Barry McHugh will need to find room late from a genuine rear position.

races.paceDynamic: Zephlyn is the lone confirmed pace-setter in this 2m Catterick handicap and, despite being a natural hold-up horse redistributed to the front, is the most likely horse to take the field along at a sustainable, uncontested gallop on Good ground — a genuine leader in the race if not by preference. With nine runners all holding hold-up profiles and several — Slack Alice, Speechman, Lillistar, Star Of Jupiter, and Ruler Of The River — being true closers mapped to midfield purely because the rear of the field is already oversubscribed, this race will be run at a measured, single-file tempo that suits horses who can travel prominently without being challenged early. The absence of genuine front-running pressure means the pace is unlikely to be severe enough to collapse late, which penalises pure hold-up horses trying to make significant ground in the home straight and favours those who can sit close to Zephlyn through the middle miles. This race shape most strongly rewards a patient but prominent-travelling profile — a horse capable of sitting second or third, conserving energy through the long Catterick circuit, and producing a sustained run from the home turn rather than a sharp late burst.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Zephlyn Leads, Closers Fail
scenarios.trigger: If Zephlyn sets a steady, uncontested pace and the filed of true closers cannot generate enough late momentum to overhaul those who tracked the leader.
scenarios.body: Zephlyn dictates from the front at a controlled tempo, and horses who can sit close — Karthala and Slack Alice, who have both placed consistently at this type of trip on good ground — pick off the front-runner in the final two furlongs; the true hold-up runners emerging from a congested midfield lack the finishing kick to reel them in.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Storms Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves slightly more honest than expected and a genuine closer finds clear daylight to finish off strongly from the rear.
scenarios.body: Free World or Fleur de Mer, both of whom have placed at this trip and going combination, finds the run of the race and hits the line late as the front group ties up; this shape requires more genuine gallop than Zephlyn's lone lead typically generates, making it the less likely but not impossible outcome.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Grind, Stamina Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the race develops into a slog from halfway, with several horses pressing Zephlyn earlier than expected, stretching the pace and exposing stamina questions.
scenarios.body: Slack Alice, a two-time winner over distances beyond 20 furlongs and showing strong form at 2m plus, thrives as the race becomes attritional; Lillistar, who has placed repeatedly over 16 furlongs on good ground, also benefits from a genuine test of stamina through the final half-mile.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, No Clear Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Zephlyn fails to stride forward naturally and multiple horses contest the early lead, creating an unusually contested pace for this field composition.
scenarios.body: A scrambled early order unsettles rhythm and produces a messy tactical race where Speechman, placed twice over this sort of trip on good ground despite coming here on just four days' rest, or Star Of Jupiter, who has placed three times on good in this range, takes advantage of the disorder with a clean run.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Zephlyn actually strides forward to lead from the gate — if Jason Hart elects to settle instead, this race has no natural pace-setter and the tempo collapses entirely, benefiting only the most prominent travellers.

Slack Alice, Speechman, Lillistar, Star Of Jupiter, and Ruler Of The River are all genuine hold-up horses compressed into midfield on the map — watch for traffic and interference entering the home straight as they all seek the same late running room simultaneously.

Free World's ⚠ fade tag combined with the likely moderate pace is a concern — if the race is run at a stop-start gallop, horses that cannot sustain their effort through the final two furlongs of this tight Catterick circuit are vulnerable regardless of early position.

Karthala's 5 places from 15 similar-going runs at 16f-20f make it the most consistent course-and-going profile in the field — watch how Sean D Bowen uses the tongue-strap run to see if the headgear change unlocks a finishing effort the form suggests is within reach.

Ruler Of The River and Speechman share the same trainer (Philip Kirby, 0/13 T14) — with both horses racing back quickly (7 and 4 days respectively) and the yard out of form, watch whether either is being run for a handicap mark rather than to win.

races.name: Hannah Blanchard 21st Birthday Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Captain Cess
runners_data.note: Has won at 6f on good recently and his form string (06-231) shows a horse coming into form; Zak Wheatley rides and Declan Carroll's yard has had a 1/7 fortnight, making this a live each-way player from a hold-up berth that should suit a strong finish on this track.

runners_data.name: Miss Rainbow
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner fitted with a visor; Connor Beasley knows her well, and her 10/15 record on similar ground with two wins underlines her suitability to these conditions — the key question is whether her 5f wins translate to 6f, but Catterick's undulations favour her style.

runners_data.name: Barmyblade
runners_data.note: Boasts a strong recent record (1-1-2 in last five on good, 4W5P on similar going) and Tim Easterby's yard is in good form at 2/79 over 14 days; a natural hold-up horse whose chance is tempered by being pushed into a midfield position, so needs a stronger pace than Miss Rainbow is likely to set.

runners_data.name: Lucius Aurelius
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's runner is a genuine prominent type stepping back to 5f-familiar ground, though his 6f record is limited; Jack Nicholls (3lb claim) gives a weight advantage, and the horse's front-running tendencies mean he is the most likely to press Miss Rainbow and shape the race from the front.

runners_data.name: Howzak
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old whose best form has come on standard/AW surfaces (1W at 6f/STA) rather than turf good, and only 2/15 on similar going with no wins on turf; Billy Garritty takes the ride but the going stats are a clear concern here.

runners_data.name: Call Glory
runners_data.note: Ian Williams has had a productive 14 days (5/40), and Call Glory's record shows consistent placing (0W4P on good) mostly at 7f — dropping to 6f and being pushed off the rail is a double disadvantage; a genuine hold-up horse who cannot get his natural position, softening his prospects materially.

runners_data.name: Enjoy The Night
runners_data.note: Seb Spencer's three-year-old carries the lowest weight (131lbs) and has form at 5f on soft/good, but is racing out of a true hold-up role in what is expected to be a single-file, controlled-pace affair; limited evidence at 6f and a 0W1P record on similar ground leaves this runner needing things to go wrong for others.

runners_data.name: Battenburg Belle
runners_data.note: Rebecca Menzies's filly has a strong place profile (1W4P on good, including a recent win at 6f/GOO) and Jason Hart is a capable jockey; she is a natural closer forced into a midfield role, but her 6f course-applicable form is arguably the best of the hold-up brigade, and she should not be ignored if any pace collapse occurs.

races.paceDynamic: Miss Rainbow is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pressing rival, Connor Beasley can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the outset over this 6f at Catterick. The field is unusually hold-up heavy — Barmyblade, Call Glory, Enjoy The Night, and Battenburg Belle are all true closers but have been mapped to midfield because the rear is oversubscribed; they are unlikely to secure their natural position and will instead race closer to the pace than ideal. Lucius Aurelius and Captain Cess represent the most credible challengers to Miss Rainbow's lead, with Lucius likely to press from a prominent berth and Captain Cess tracking from just off the pace. With one controlled front-runner setting a measured tempo on good ground, this race shape strongly favours hold-up and prominent horses who can produce a decisive late burst — but because so many closers will be shuffled forward out of role, the runner most likely to exploit the pace advantage is the horse who travels smoothly in second or third and pounces from a position of comfort rather than a genuine late swoop.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Miss Rainbow Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Miss Rainbow is allowed to stride clear uncontested and set a fair-to-modest tempo through the early stages.
scenarios.body: Beasley settles Miss Rainbow in a rhythm, stretches the field into a single file on the Catterick straight, and her course form and good-ground record make her very hard to pass; OR=58 and visor-equipped, she looks the dominant shape player here. Lucius Aurelius, tracking in second, is best placed to mount a challenge if the pace eases but must find improvement at 6f.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Challenger Overpowers Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Lucius Aurelius or Captain Cess travels powerfully in the slipstream and picks off Miss Rainbow inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A genuine prominent type who has tracked the controlled pace throughout gets a slingshot run off the final bend and has enough gas to collar a potentially tiring leader; Catterick's downhill finish rewards those who travel well and save one last effort. Captain Cess's recent 6f win on good and Lucius Aurelius's prominent style make both live candidates for this scenario.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Rush From True Closers
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is faster than expected and the field strings out, creating enough of a tempo for genuine hold-up horses to power home.
scenarios.body: Barmyblade has the best recent form (101 record) among the closers and, if able to find a clear run despite racing out of his natural rear position, could arrive with a late flourish; Battenburg Belle's consistent placing record at 6f on good gives her a similar profile. Both are disadvantaged by racing closer than ideal, so this shape requires a tempo lift to materialise.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Field Bunches
scenarios.trigger: If Miss Rainbow fades sharply in the final furlong having set a muddling gallop and the race deteriorates into a sprint finish.
scenarios.body: A bunched finish would theoretically open the door for any of the midfield horses but, crucially, those mapped there are true hold-up types racing out of role and unlikely to find an explosive turn of foot from a forward position; in this chaotic shape, Battenburg Belle's proven 6f form and Howzak's occasional ability to land a blow at a big price are the marginal picks.

watchPoints.text: Miss Rainbow (visor, Connor Beasley) is uncontested at the front — watch whether Beasley deliberately sets a slow tempo to conserve energy through the 6f, as this would extinguish any genuine closing run and make her almost impossible to reel in.

Lucius Aurelius is the only horse likely to press Miss Rainbow early; if Jack Nicholls (3) can slot in directly behind and travel smoothly, he becomes the chief danger to the leader at the top of the home straight.

Barmyblade's outstanding good-ground record (4W5P) makes him the standout closer on form, but he must race further forward than ideal — watch how Sean Kirrane positions him in the first two furlongs, as failing to get cover could use his horse's energy too early.

Battenburg Belle has placed in five of her last six on good ground at 6f and Jason Hart is an experienced handler of tricky races; if the pace quickens at the two-furlong pole, she is the hold-up horse most likely to arrive with a meaningful late effort despite her positional disadvantage.

Howzak's going record on turf-good is poor (0W0P in 2 turf-good starts) contrasted with his AW wins — monitor market moves for any support, as drifting odds would confirm punter concern about conditions.

races.name: Racingtv.com Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Brunello Breeze
runners_data.note: Returning from 146 days off with a modest form string and a single win from 15 runs on similar ground; genuinely races from the rear and will need a strong pace and a clear passage that this race shape is unlikely to generate.

runners_data.name: On The Bubble
runners_data.note: Best recent form includes a second over 1m4f on Good ground 15 days ago, giving it the freshest credentials at the trip; its natural instinct is to race from behind, and the crowded back-end of this field makes finding clear air a real challenge.

runners_data.name: Halimede
runners_data.note: Lightly raced three-year-old from the powerful Sir Mark Prescott yard whose T14 strike rate of 9/28 demands respect; all three career runs came at 8f on Standard, flagged as a fader in the finish, and stepping up to 1m4f on Good is a significant unknown.

runners_data.name: Hansteen
runners_data.note: The race-shaper — won over 1m4f on Good and placed at similar distances, with Jason Hart likely to use his natural front-running role to control tempo; a sustained gallop with no rival to pressure him suits his chance considerably.

runners_data.name: Muhib
runners_data.note: Consistent performer at 1m2f-1m4f on Good ground with four places from six recent runs, though a natural hold-up horse who will be racing out of his preferred rear position given the volume of closers in the field; the style compromise is the main obstacle to winning.

runners_data.name: Project Kinsman
runners_data.note: Philip Kirby handler running two in the race; has placed over 1m2f on Good ground and showed improvement stepping up in trip, but like Muhib is a genuine closer repositioned to midfield by the race shape, which tempers its winning prospects.

runners_data.name: N'Ion
runners_data.note: A five-time apprentice rider on board this three-year-old who has faded in finishes and shows just one placing from five runs on similar going; mapped out of natural position and has done nothing in form to suggest it can overcome those twin obstacles.

runners_data.name: Spirit Of Tokyo
runners_data.note: Second Kirby runner, four runs showing a declining form string with no win and modest finishing positions; a natural hold-up horse racing out of role, and with limited experience and no strong form angle, is up against it here.

races.paceDynamic: Hansteen is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rivals to challenge him, will likely dictate terms from the outset at a controlled, sustainable gallop over this 1m4f trip on Good ground at Catterick. The remainder of the field — On The Bubble, Muhib, Project Kinsman, N'Ion and Spirit Of Tokyo — are all true hold-up horses redistributed into midfield positions simply because the map cannot accommodate that many genuine closers at the rear, meaning their actual racing patterns will compress the midfield rather than create any secondary pressure on Hansteen. Brunello Breeze and Halimede also sit at the back of the field, reinforcing a scenario where Hansteen controls the race virtually unchallenged through the early and middle stages. This race shape strongly favours horses capable of tracking the leader from a prominent position and sustaining their effort through the final two furlongs, as genuine hold-up horses face the compounded problem of an uncontested pace and a compressed midfield through which to find a clear run.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hansteen Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Hansteen is allowed to dictate an uncontested lead and sets a measured pace that suits his stamina profile.
scenarios.body: Hansteen rolls along in front with no pressure applied, reaching the home straight with a stack of petrol in reserve and simply extending clear as the hold-up runners struggle to mount a clean challenge from a congested midfield. Horses that have tracked him closely from second or third will benefit most, as the pace will not be strong enough to bring late finishers into play.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Midfield Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Hansteen sets a pace just strong enough to string the field out, allowing one well-positioned hold-up horse to thread through for a clean run.
scenarios.body: With the field spread across the track, a horse positioned three or four lengths off the leader in the first half of the race avoids the midfield scrum and arrives with a clear passage entering the final furlong. Muhib's consistent placed form at this trip on Good ground and Project Kinsman's course form make them the most plausible beneficiaries, despite both being squeezed out of their natural rear-of-field berth.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Tires Late
scenarios.trigger: If Hansteen sets a fraction quicker than intended and the field is restrained early, leaving him vulnerable inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A faster-than-expected early pace drains Hansteen's reserves through the final climb, opening the door for a closer with a clean outside run to reel him in late. Given the number of redistributed hold-up horses crowding the midfield, only one or two will find daylight in time, making this scenario dependent on traffic luck as much as stamina.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Complete Upset — Rear Closer
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses entirely and a true hold-up horse produced very late catches a tiring field in the final strides.
scenarios.body: This requires both Hansteen to slow dramatically and the midfield bottleneck to clear sufficiently for a deep-seated closer to find clear racing room, both of which are low-probability events in the same race. Brunello Breeze, returning from 146 days off with form at the trip, and N'Ion are the most natural fit for this shape, but their recent records and fitness questions make a winning outcome unlikely.

watchPoints.text: Hansteen (Jason Hart) — watch whether he is allowed to bowl along unchallenged from the off; if he hits the front and settles, he could prove very hard to peg back at this trip on Good ground.

Midfield traffic — with five horses all naturally wanting to race from the rear compressed into the middle of the pack, watch for significant crowding and scrubbing along from the 5f pole as jockeys scramble for clear runs.

Muhib — despite racing out of natural position, its consistent placed record at 1m2f-1m4f on Good makes it the most dangerous challenger if Warren Fentiman (3lb claim) can secure a pitch just off the leader early rather than being swallowed by the midfield group.

Halimede (Sir Mark Prescott) — Prescott's 9/28 T14 strike rate is notable; watch market moves on this unexposed three-year-old stepping up sharply in trip, as stable form can mask a well-prepared improver despite the fading flag.

On The Bubble — ran just 15 days ago and placed over this exact trip on Good ground; if it can overcome the positional disadvantage and find a clear outside run turning in, its recent course-relevant form makes it one to note in any scenario where Hansteen weakens.

races.name: Racing Again 17th August Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Without Flaw
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with a solid Good-ground record (11/15, 1W2P on similar going) and fresh enough at 7 days since last run; Warren Fentiman's 3lb claim helps at the weights from OR 53, and the horse's tendency to track the pace closely makes this race shape very compatible.

runners_data.name: Brain Freeze
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse with the best recent form figures in the field, including a win on Good ground, and Connor Beasley gives it a significant jockey upgrade; the visor (hg:v) suggests a need for focus and the horse's closing style is reliant on a strong gallop that may not fully materialise here.

runners_data.name: Doralee
runners_data.note: David & Nicola Barron send out a consistent prominent type who has placed four times on similar going in 15 attempts — no wins in recent form (latest run was a 2nd) but reliability in position is its strength; Jason Hart is an experienced handler of pace, though T14 at 0/8 tempers stable confidence.

runners_data.name: Havin A Flyer
runners_data.note: The race's sole front-runner, setting up the entire pace dynamic; tongue-tie (hg:t) noted, and the critical concern is that all five recent runs came on AW Southwell/standard surfaces, making this first turf Good outing the key unknown — if he handles the switch, he controls the race.

runners_data.name: Gwen Tennyson
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with limited recent form (best recent finish a 3rd on Good) and apprentice William Pyle in the saddle; at OR 49 with T14 2/19, the trainer angle is lukewarm and in a race shape dominated by front-runners it would need significant improvement to feature.

runners_data.name: Mimime
runners_data.note: Lightly raced with just three runs on record, all at 6f — dropping to 5f for the first time raises a legitimate trip query, and its natural tendency to fade in the finish is flagged; shown in midfield on the map because the field's hold-up contingent is too large to place all at the rear, so its true rearward inclination is likely to leave it further back than ideal.

runners_data.name: Dunnington Lad
runners_data.note: Veteran 6-year-old with a fair Good-ground sample (12/15) but no wins and only one place from hold-up tactics; Peter Winks at 0/1 T14 and Shay Farmer's 5lb claim are modest assets — placed in midfield on the map because hold-up positions are oversubscribed, but its natural style means it will likely drift toward the back, and STYLE_FIT 0.91 tempers its chance meaningfully.

races.paceDynamic: Havin A Flyer is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no natural rival to press for the lead, should dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the off on Good ground over this sharp 5f at Catterick. Without Flaw and Doralee will look to track closely from a prominent berth, likely sitting just off the leader's quarters through the first two furlongs, meaning the pace won't be truly searchingly fast. The result is a race run at a measured but honest clip that will suit horses able to travel prominently and kick from the front or near it, rather than those needing a truly breakneck tempo to close from behind. This shape strongly favours the lead-to-prominent profile — Havin A Flyer, Without Flaw and Doralee are best placed structurally, while the field holds more hold-up types than can operate from their natural position: Mimime and Dunnington Lad, both true hold-up horses, have been redistributed to midfield on the map because they are unlikely to secure their preferred rear position, and this further concentrates advantage toward the pace-pressing runners.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Havin A Flyer Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Havin A Flyer breaks smartly and dictates an uncontested, measured gallop, controlling tempo throughout.
scenarios.body: Havin A Flyer sets every fraction and, on Good ground at a track that rewards front-runners over 5f, simply has too much in hand for rivals to reel in; the hold-up horses are structurally compromised and can't generate the closing momentum they need.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Overhaul
scenarios.trigger: If Without Flaw or Doralee track Havin A Flyer tightly and sustain their effort to collar the leader inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Good going suits both Without Flaw (sim-going record 11/15, 1W2P) and Doralee (12/15, 1W4P), and if Havin A Flyer has given slightly too much in front, either prominent runner has the positional advantage to pounce; Jason Hart on Doralee and Warren Fentiman on Without Flaw both have the tactical awareness to bide their time in a pocket and strike late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Closes
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than anticipated and the front-runners tie each other up, leaving a gap for a hold-up horse to finish through.
scenarios.body: Brain Freeze has genuine Good-ground form (5/5, 1W3P sim-going) and Connor Beasley the experience to find a late split, making it the most credible finisher from off the pace if conditions allow; however, Mimime and Dunnington Lad are true hold-up types repositioned on the map and face an uphill task getting involved unless the race truly falls apart up front.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Scrambles Field
scenarios.trigger: If there is a poor break, crowding early, or Havin A Flyer misses the kick and the field fans out with no clear pace control.
scenarios.body: Without the settled rhythm that suits the map's dominant shape, the race becomes a lottery and any horse capable of grabbing a handy position opportunistically — particularly Gwen Tennyson or Brain Freeze — could snatch an unlikely result; Havin A Flyer's recent AW form raises a small flag about course-surface transition if the horse is unsettled by the switch to turf Good.

watchPoints.text: Watch Havin A Flyer at the start — if it misses the break or fails to establish the lead immediately, the entire pace map collapses and the race opens up unpredictably for the prominent horses.

Monitor Havin A Flyer's early behaviour on turf Good — all five career runs were on AW Southwell/standard, and any surface-related unsettlement in the first furlong could compromise its ability to control the pace.

Mimime's first attempt at 5f (previously 6f only) makes it vulnerable to being found out by the trip, particularly given its flagged tendency to fade in the finish — watch for it dropping away from two furlongs out.

Brain Freeze with the visor applied is worth watching in-running — if Connor Beasley can position it closer than its natural hold-up style suggests, it has the form to be a factor, but a wide draw or slow pace will neutralise it entirely.

Without Flaw's 7-day turnaround and Warren Fentiman's 3lb claim are worth tracking in the market — any significant support in a field where the prominent profile dominates would reinforce it as the most likely beneficiary if Havin A Flyer weakens late.
